state: Record an initial architecture for a Can-owned test suite; the user suggests reusing Can execution under generic native supervision. The author is an AI coding agent, making explicit contracts, reliable synthesis and focused diagnosis the design criteria rather than ease of human typing. Arbitrary ordinary Can helpers must work. Can must own scenario sequences, expected answers, execution policy and reporting, replacing authored host harnesses while allowing native mechanics. Retained coverage, independent facts, bounded laptop storage/load and cleanup are mandatory; compatibility with old language details is not. Work is design-only, excluding live tests, builds and measurements. Can currently lowers to TypeScript executed by Bun, and exposes checked IR without a discovered general interpreter. A new interpreter would need complete callable/identity and error-occurrence semantics, supplied fixture behavior, coordination, ownership and reachable platform bindings; changing executor does not supply browser/DB capabilities or process containment. The Go assertion supervisor provides separate Bun launches, external time budgets, bounded diagnostics and leased generation validation. It is still assertion-specific and does not establish the proposed live protocol or comprehensive descendant, filesystem and remote-resource enforcement. Concrete functions have mandatory offline supplied roots. All declarations are checked before optional root selection; proposed focused development verification selects a conservative case/helper/fixture closure, uses all roots on ambiguity and labels partial evidence. Qualification remains all-root, all-obligation and all-required-environment work. One arrangement uses an outer generic Go supervisor, a Can controller and Can worker processes sharing one reference-built suite artifact. Policy and verdicts stay Can-owned; native code performs enforcement, factual transport and cleanup and refuses an incomplete completion receipt. Candidate children must lack the runner's private reporting channel. There are no measured startup or load results comparing fresh processes, persistent workers or same-process threads. A trust contract needs separate compiler/runtime/supervisor identities for the reference and compiler/runtime identities for the candidate. The suite may be compiled once by a qualified reference toolchain and reconstructed in every worker, while the candidate produces only test subjects. New suite syntax/APIs unsupported by the reference require a blocked run or independent reviewed refresh, not fallback to candidate compilation. Refresh uses available predecessor checks, independent fixed vectors and failing controls before deliberate promotion; the initial reference is an explicit trusted seed, not a circularly established proof. Candidate self-rebuild is an additional subject comparison. Other choices use candidate-built suite code with control comparisons or restrict runs to a frozen independently distributed suite artifact. Production-codegen/runtime/browser claims still require actual candidate artifacts under a future interpreter, and common frontend/runtime errors remain possible. Reuse artifacts only within owned runs by default, keeping compact provenance rather than full private caches and disposable trees. A full interpreter can be reconsidered for a funded language-wide purpose, valuable semantic diversity, or established execution-backend cost/debugging limitations after bounded remedies. Emitted TypeScript alone does not justify it.

backend.instructions: Choose the first execution implementation for these native Can tests.

criteria.existing_can: Reuse Can's existing compiled execution path under native containment, preserving ordinary semantics while designing the absent runner APIs.
criteria.full_interpreter: Make a full Can interpreter the initial executor, accepting the additional runtime semantics, bindings and supervision work.
criteria.new_codegen: Implement another compiled native Can executor initially, providing all ordinary language and platform semantics plus containment.

worker_boundary.instructions: Which execution boundary should each case attempt receive initially?

criteria.fresh_process: Give every case/variant attempt its own disposable Bun process under the outer supervisor, separate from the controller, initially running one case at a time.
criteria.process_pool: Adopt persistent process workers with explicit reset contracts and leakage checks before reuse, reducing launch repetition but increasing lifetime coupling.
criteria.same_process_workers: Place case attempts in threads of a shared Bun process, adding state-isolation rules and external termination of the process when local interruption fails.

trust_relationship.instructions: How should the initial architecture establish who compiles the authoritative test logic?

criteria.reference_builds_suite: Compile authoritative suite code with the selected reference toolchain and isolate candidate outputs as subjects; qualify reference changes separately and never silently fall back to candidate-built judges.
criteria.candidate_with_controls: Build the judge using the candidate, supplement it with independent controls and comparisons, and explicitly account for incomplete detection of candidate defects in the judge.
criteria.frozen_suite_artifact: Use a fixed independently accepted suite executable as the test authority, with out-of-band source updates and the resulting constraints on rapid test changes.
